title: Voice mode — the assistant speaks
why: Give Squid-OS a spoken channel: responses, errors, and system events are read aloud via the local squid-tts server, toggleable live, interruptible at any time.
outcomes: /voice + alt+v toggle; per-language voice settings; sentence-chunk streaming with ~2s time-to-first-audio; universal alt+x shut-up scoped to speech groups; sponge key-down cancellation via 'squid-os voice stop'; bilingual alert lead-ins driven by last-user-language detection.

milestones.name: Core voice pipeline
pattern: Single-owner voice coordinator with group bumping; chunking strategy behind an interface
milestones.objective: Assistant responses are spoken in sentence chunks while streaming, with per-language voice selection, group-scoped cancellation, and clean process teardown.
milestones.success: With voice on, first audio arrives ~2s into a response; alt+x silences the whole group instantly including not-yet-emitted chunks; no orphaned aplay processes; kill switch verified under race.
milestones.diagram:
flowchart LR
Stream[Assistant stream] --> Chunker
Chunker --> Coord[Coordinator]
Coord --> Detect[/detect]
Detect --> Lookup[Voice lookup]
Lookup --> CLI[squid-tts-say]
CLI --> Aplay[aplay]
AltX[alt+x] -->|CancelGroup| Coord

tasks.name: Add voice settings
tasks.what: Add nested voice config (enabled, voices.en, voices.fr) with defaults enabled=false, en=jane, fr=jane; normalize missing/partial sections at load time in internal/config/settings.go.
tasks.why: Everything else reads from this structure; defaults must exist before the wrapper.
acceptance: Missing voice section loads as disabled with jane/jane
Partial sections (only voices.en set) fill fr from default
Invalid voice names pass through (server validates at request time)

tasks.name: Build voice wrapper and coordinator
tasks.what: New internal/voice package: Speak(text, cfg) spawns squid-tts-say in its own process group (detect → voice lookup → pipe stdin); Coordinator owns group state (StartGroup/Emit/EndGroup/CancelGroup) with muted-drop, back-to-back within group, and bump-across-groups via an onPreempt policy hook.
tasks.why: Single owner of detect → lookup → spawn → teardown AND group arbitration; every caller goes through it; the onPreempt hook keeps the door open to stacking later.
snippet:
// Spawn: exec.Command("squid-tts-say", "-v", name, "-q", "--stdin")
// SysProcAttr{Setpgid: true}; kill(-pgid, SIGKILL) on cancel or replacement
acceptance: Resolves voice per detected language; unknown language falls back without failing
Same-group chunks play back-to-back without bumping each other (ordering test)
Cross-group Emit bumps the playing group (default policy) and starts immediately
Cancellation mid-playback kills the whole process group; no orphaned aplay — deterministic subprocess test plus go test -race
Emit for a muted groupID is dropped even if it arrives after cancellation (late-chunk test)
Server down returns error, never panics, bounded timeout; CLI resolved from PATH

tasks.name: Implement the Chunker
tasks.what: Define Chunker { Feed; Flush; ArmHoldTimer } in internal/voice with a sentence-boundary strategy: split on . ! ? \n, hold fragments under ~3 words and merge, max hold 1.5s via owned timer, max chunk ~40 words force-flush.
tasks.why: Measured TTS floor is 2-4s per call — single-word chunks sound robotic; merging fixes bullet lists; the interface keeps the algorithm swappable without touching wrapper or cancellation code.
acceptance: Prose emits per sentence; one-word bullets merge into groups
40-word run-on without periods force-flushes
Held fragment emits via timer when input stalls (injected ticker test)
Flush drains buffer exactly once; Feed after Flush starts fresh; timer cancelled after Flush
Strategy params (min words, max hold, max size, boundaries) are constructor args

tasks.name: Wire narration into the assistant stream
tasks.what: Allocate a group ID at assistant message start; feed rendered text deltas into the Chunker and Emit chunks to the coordinator; EndGroup at stream end; group lifecycle tied to the message, surviving UIStreamState.reset() around tools.
tasks.why: This is the core UX — first audio ~2s, not after full generation; already-emitted chunks keep playing during tool calls (no pause concept exists).
acceptance: First chunk speaks while later sentences are still generating
Stream end sends EndGroup; a muted group stops receiving feeds (producer checks coordinator before emitting)
Group survives UIStreamState.reset() between tool phases; no duplicate or lost chunks across the reset
Voice mute never cancels the model stream or tool execution (independent contexts verified)
Session switch / shutdown tears down active groups (kill + indicator cleared)

tasks.name: Toggle: /voice command, alt+v, help entry
tasks.what: Register /voice on|off in internal/app/command.go (add argument handling to the name-only callbacks); bind alt+v mirroring thinking; add both keys to the hard-coded help list in internal/ui/help.go; print feedback line on toggle.
tasks.why: Live control without restarting; parity with thinking UX; WithHelp alone will not show the entry because help.go is hard-coded.
snippet:
Thinking: key.NewBinding(key.WithKeys("alt+t"), key.WithHelp("alt+t", "toggle thinking")),
Voice:    key.NewBinding(key.WithKeys("alt+v"), key.WithHelp("alt+v", "toggle voice"))
acceptance: alt+v and /voice both flip the same runtime state; settings value is the startup source of truth; runtime toggle does not write the settings file
Help overlay lists alt+v
Toggling off mid-speech kills current playback immediately (CancelGroup + disable)

tasks.name: Speaking indicator
tasks.what: Show a speaker glyph / 'speaking…' in the existing status row (internal/ui/notification.go:98, called from render.go:78) while any audio plays; cleared on completion or cancellation.
tasks.why: Shut-up needs a visible target; users must see that voice is active and that alt+x did something.
acceptance: Indicator appears on first chunk start, disappears on player exit or kill
Never stuck on after cancellation (kill path clears it)
Stale callbacks from superseded groups cannot clear a NEWER group's indicator (generation-ID guard)

milestones.name: Cancellation and external control
pattern: Group-scoped cancellation; external commands route into the same coordinator
milestones.objective: alt+x, new messages, and sponge key-down all trigger the identical CancelGroup path; 'squid-os voice stop' works from outside the TUI.
milestones.success: Every cancel source silences the whole group within one frame and leaves no orphans; socket command round-trips like input ops.
milestones.diagram:
flowchart LR
AltX[alt+x] --> Coord[Coordinator]
NewMsg[Submitted message] --> Coord
Sponge[Sponge key-down] --> CLI2[squid-os voice stop]
CLI2 --> Socket[Unix socket]
Socket --> Coord
Coord --> KillPG[kill -pgid SIGKILL]
AltX -. CancelGroup .-> Coord
NewMsg -. CancelGroup .-> Coord
Socket -. CancelGroup .-> Coord

tasks.name: alt+x universal shut-up
tasks.what: Bind alt+x (verified free); handler calls coordinator.CancelGroup(activeGroup) — kills running chunk, drops buffered chunks, mutes all future chunks of that group. Handler must run BEFORE mode dispatch (internal/app/input.go:15) so authorization and help overlays cannot swallow the key.
tasks.why: Per-group mute with zero exception rules; applies to narration AND alerts identically; one press silences a multi-chunk error completely. Not sticky: next group speaks normally.
acceptance: alt+x during narration mutes rest of current message only — including phrases not yet emitted
alt+x during an error lead-in silences the upcoming detail chunk too (one press, whole group dead)
alt+x works while the authorization overlay or help overlay is open
Next assistant message/alert speaks normally without re-enabling anything

tasks.name: New submitted message cancels speech
tasks.what: Submitting a user message cancels the active group before processing begins, hooked at ALL THREE admission paths: idle keyboard (stream.go:86), queued keyboard (queued_input.go:39), and socket admission (local_input.go:42) — at admission, not eventual delivery.
tasks.why: User talking/typing a new instruction = barge-in; busy socket submissions currently push no UI event (local_input.go:59-62), so hooking only delivery misses immediate cancellation.
acceptance: Sending a message while Jane speaks silences her whole group before the new turn starts, from all three paths
Plain typing WITHOUT submitting does NOT cancel (listen-while-drafting preserved)

tasks.name: squid-os voice stop CLI command
tasks.what: New internal/cli/voice.go following the input.go pattern: 'squid-os voice stop' sends a socket op to the live TUI triggering the same CancelGroup as alt+x; register in cli.go, add op to server dispatch (internal/localinput/server.go:188) and app-side handler (internal/app/local_input.go). Scaffold for future on/off subcommands.
tasks.why: Sponge needs key-down cancellation before any transcript exists; same Unix socket protocol as input, zero new infrastructure. Use existing --instance/--session flags (input.go:46-47).
snippet:
// voice stop = localinput.Request{Op: "voice_stop"}
// reply: {status: "cancelled" | "nothing_playing"}, exit 0 either way
acceptance: 'squid-os voice stop' against a live instance silences the current group; reply acknowledges actual cancellation or explicit nothing-playing no-op, exit 0
No live instance gives clean error, non-zero exit, same style as input commands
--instance/--session flags behave like input's

tasks.name: Sponge key-down integration
tasks.what: In the sponge client, on shortcut key-DOWN (before transcription), invoke 'squid-os voice stop'. LOCATE the sponge source first (check ~/src/squid-stack/squid-companion and the sponge repo) and record the real path here before implementing.
tasks.why: Voice must die the instant the user starts talking into the mic — not when the transcript arrives seconds later; speaking over the assistant would be unusable.
files: ~ squid-stack/squid-tray/squid_sponge.py (LOCATED: sponge client lives at /home/goglue/src/squid-stack/squid-tray/squid_sponge.py, not a separate repo)
acceptance: Pressing the sponge shortcut while voice plays silences it within ~100ms, before any audio from the user is captured
Works even when no voice is playing (no-op, no error spam)

milestones.name: Bilingual alerts
pattern: Event hooks push preformatted alert groups through the same coordinator
milestones.objective: Errors, authorization prompts, context bust, skill loads, sub-agent calls, and thinking-start are announced in the user's language with English detail where relevant.
milestones.success: Each event speaks its lead-in in lastUserLang as its own group; all alerts share universal cancellation; alert map lives in one table of ~12 strings.
milestones.diagram:
flowchart LR
Events[App events] --> Format[Alert formatter]
LastLang[lastUserLang] --> Format
Format -->|StartGroup| Coord[Coordinator]

tasks.name: Track lastUserLang asynchronously
tasks.what: On every user message submission, fire /detect asynchronously (goroutine, ~500ms deadline) with a submission ID; store the result in session state only if that ID is still the newest. Fallback: previous value, then en.
tasks.why: Drives alert lead-in language (~75ms locally, cheap enough to run always) without serializing any of the three submission paths; older results must never overwrite newer language state.
acceptance: French user message sets lastUserLang=fr for subsequent alerts
Rapid-fire two messages (FR then EN): only the EN result lands, even if FR resolves second (ordering test)
Detect failure/timeout leaves previous value intact; turn latency unaffected

tasks.name: Alert map and formatting
tasks.what: Single table of bilingual alert templates in internal/voice/alerts.go: error, authorization, context-bust, skill-loaded with name, sub-agent-called, thinking-started; formatter picks language from lastUserLang and interpolates details.
tasks.why: ~12 strings total — maintainable; the user hears their own language immediately while technical detail stays English (auto-detected by the server).
snippet:
var alerts = map[Event]map[string]string{
    Error:        {en: "An error occurred.", fr: "Une erreur est survenue."},
    Authorization:{en: "A command requires your authorization.", fr: "Une commande requiert votre autorisation."},
    ContextBust:  {en: "Warning, no context left.", fr: "Attention, plus de contexte disponible."},
    SkillLoaded:  {en: "I loaded the skill {name}.", fr: "Jai charge la competence {name}."},
    SubAgent:     {en: "I sent a sub-agent working on it.", fr: "Jai lance un sous-agent qui va effectuer le travail."},
    ThinkingStart:{en: "Let me think about it now.", fr: "Laisse-moi y penser."},
}
acceptance: Each event renders the exact EN/FR strings from the table
Error alerts append raw English detail after the lead-in (same group)
Unknown language falls back to EN templates

tasks.name: Hook events into the voice coordinator
tasks.what: Wire all six alert call sites, each starting its own group: ToolEventNeedAuth (stream.go:293), LoadedSkill (stream.go:284/310), a NEW pre-execution agent event in tool_worker.go (ToolEventRunning fires too late, after ExecuteTools returns), error paths with distinct context-bust classification, and thinking-start (once per thinking session when thinking mode is active).
tasks.why: These are the 'get my eyes here' moments — the highest-value voice use; alerts land between messages in practice, so bumping narration is the rare overlap case.
snippet:
// guard: coordinator suppresses new alerts while an alert is playing
// (prevents TTS-failure -> spoken-error recursion)
acceptance: With voice on each of the six events speaks its alert as its own group; with voice off silence and no behavior change
Thinking-start speaks exactly once per thinking session, only when thinking mode is active
Alert landing while the tail of an answer is still playing bumps the tail (intended behavior) and speaks
alt+x during an alert behaves identically to alt+x during narration (whole group dies including pending detail chunk)
TTS failure during an alert produces no further speech (recursion guard tested)
